candidate_relations.reason: Urinalysis was normal, so UTI with bacteremia conflicts with mediport cultures growing gram-positive rods.
Hypomagnesemia of 0.66 mmol/L explains why a mediport exists, not the gram-positive-rod bacteremia.
Bacteremia due to gram-positive rods is microbiologically true but omits Williamsia spongiae/serinedens/deligens identified by 16S intent.
Bacteremia is the parent bloodstream-infection state and lacks the Williamsia species.
Fever, chills, and leukocytosis can be called sepsis but omit the line-related Williamsia bacteremia.
Neurogenic bladder–associated UTI is contradicted by a normal urinalysis and by mediport-positive cultures.
Chronic hypomagnesemia is the infusion indication, not the CDC-sequenced bacteremia.
CLABSI correctly identifies the mediport as the source after peripheral cultures cleared, but not the Williamsia species.
No murmur, vegetation, or prolonged peripheral bacteremia is described; follow-up peripheral cultures were negative at five days.
Neurogenic bladder is a urologic comorbidity, not the bloodstream infection.
Urinary tract infection is excluded by a normal urinalysis despite left-flank discomfort.
Catheter-related bloodstream infection matches mediport-positive gram-positive rods but still omits the Williamsia identification.
Infected mediport names the device source (cultures positive at three days) without the Williamsia taxon.
Prior right nephrectomy for a pelvic kidney is remote history, not the present port bacteremia.
Corynebacterium is a related coryneform gram-positive rod that 16S sequencing was sent to distinguish from Williamsia.
Renal agenesis is incorrect; the kidney was removed because it was a nonfunctioning pelvic kidney.
Bacillus species is another gram-positive rod that could be mis-assigned before 16S, not the Williamsia result sought from CDC.
Propionibacterium/Cutibacterium is a different anaerobic gram-positive rod from the aerobic actinomycete Williamsia group.

case_quality_flags: 16S rRNA sequencing was sent to CDC, but the Williamsia species result is not actually reported in the record.
